content: 1. Nystatin is not intended for the treatment of systemic fungal infections. If a patient experiences sensitization or irritation during its use, the treatment should be discontinued immediately. 2. No long-term animal studies have been conducted to assess the carcinogenic potential of nystatin. Additionally, there have been no studies to evaluate its mutagenicity or its effects on fertility in either males or females. 3. Regarding pregnancy, nystatin is classified as Category C. Animal reproduction studies have not been performed with nystatin. It is also unknown whether nystatin can cause harm to a fetus when administered to a pregnant woman or whether it can affect reproductive capacity. Nystatin should only be prescribed to a pregnant woman if it is clearly necessary. 4. It is not known whether nystatin is excreted in human breast milk. Since many drugs are excreted in human milk, caution should be exercised when nystatin is administered to a nursing mother.
